_note: #1186 — set B, VERSIONED WITH THE RULES (12 files: top p1..p8, bottom p1..p4 — the bottom posts four programs now, where 1114-1 had three). vs tableVersion 1114-1 the picker ranks every chain by the time it will really take (#1186 rule 1: each step at the feed row its cutter actually runs, plus the priced bit changes) and keeps one cutter per shape and diameter (#1186 rule 6); every flat may now propose as a primary. What changed, and why: top p2 is the ⌀1 × 7 flat cutting the curved remainder (15 ops, 33 min 3 s where it cut 14 s — the regions only the small flat reaches; the rank puts coverage before price); top p5's curved rough moved to the XCAN 1.5 × 8 (11 min 13 s against the 1.5 × 6's 16 min 33 s, whose own row is dearer — and rule 6 kept the longer flute); top p6's finish runs on the ⌀3.175 ball × 22 instead of the × 10 (rule 6's one ball per diameter; 6 min either way); the bottom's primary moved to the ⌀3.175 × 42 O-flute (2 h 8 min against the ×12 metal O-flute's 2 h 21 min), the curved rough is its own program on the TiN corn ⌀3.0 × 12 (45 min 1 s), and the rest runs on the Ucheer ⌀2 × 15 instead of the ⌀2 × 12 (rule 6; 1 h 49 min against 1 h 26 min — the known, non-unsafe cost carried on #1186 until the setup-boundary gate lands). The top's freeing contour (p8, 14 min 47 s on the ⌀3.175 × 42) and every other program are byte-identical to 1114-1. The e2e reads this table as the cross-door check.
rule: #1186 (the planner's one currency, 2026-11-10) + #1192 (the proposal shortlist). (a) A CANDIDATE CHAIN IS RANKED BY THE TIME IT WILL REALLY TAKE: every step is priced at the feed row the cutter ACTUALLY runs — its own, or the borrowed row the CAM resolves — plus the priced bit changes (#1114); heuristics only propose, and ties go to fewer bit changes, then owned before catalogue. (b) EVERY FLAT MAY PROPOSE AS A PRIMARY (the maximal-flat gate is gone); the candidate set is shortlisted to the incumbent (the largest flat) and the best own-row removal-rate flat, every other flat staying a rest/finish candidate. (c) ONE CUTTER PER SHAPE AND DIAMETER AT THE JOB LEVEL: the longest stated reach does the work, and a shorter sibling is kept only where the longest would borrow. The setup-boundary refinement (a one-setup job keeps every sibling) is #1195-blocked and NOT in this build.
